title: Treating TB in children
dek: Higher mg/kg, child-friendly FDCs, SHINE for non-severe DS, adult-type regimens when they have adult-type disease, and Pa-sparing DR constructs under 14.
story: Children are not small adults in the intensive-care sense, but a 16-year-old with a cavity is pharmacologically closer to Study 31 than to a 9-month-old with a Ghon focus. WHO child dosing uses higher mg/kg than adult caps (INH ~10 mg/kg, RIF ~15 mg/kg, PZA ~35 mg/kg, EMB ~20 mg/kg — weight bands, not napkin maths).

DS non-severe: SHINE 4-month. DS severe pulmonary: 6-month HRZ(E). TBM/osteoarticular: longer, sometimes intensified. RR/MDR under 14: BPaLM evidence is thin; 2025 BDLLfxC and all-oral BDQ/DLM-based regimens are the designed path. TPT: 3HR is the child-friendly short course; 3HP exists down to certain ages with dispersible RPT when available.
Always treat the child’s disease using the source case’s DST when the child’s own NAAT is negative. That single habit outperforms a dozen negative gastric aspirates.
deep: Dispersible FDCs exist so you do not quarter adult 600 mg RIF tablets into a 6 kg infant.
Ethambutol optic neuropathy monitoring is impractical in toddlers — still use EMB when the algorithm says so, at correct mg/kg.
BDQ and DLM have pediatric weight-band tables. Off-label crushing without PK is how you get mystery failures.
IRIS in children with HIV exists. ART timing follows the same two-week / TBM 4–8 week logic.

example.title: Infant of an RR, FQ-S mother
example.setup: 4-month-old, miliary picture, stool Ultra not detected, mother on BPaLM with gyrA WT.

steps.title: Treat as RR-TB
steps.body: The infant’s negative stool does not make this DS. Source DST is the result.

steps.title: Not adult BPaLM by default
steps.body: Age <14: BDLLfxC-class or NTP pediatric DR protocol with BDQ/DLM weight bands.

steps.title: TBM check
steps.body: Miliary infants have CNS disease until you look. LP, steroids if TBM.

example.takeaway: Pediatric TB therapy is severity + source DST + weight bands.

check.prompt: Compared with adult capped doses, WHO pediatric INH/RIF mg/kg bands are:
choices: Much lower because children are fragile
Higher mg/kg (child-specific bands), not adult 5/10 mg/kg caps scaled by eye
Zero because BCG is sufficient treatment
check.answer: Higher mg/kg (child-specific bands), not adult 5/10 mg/kg caps scaled by eye

check.prompt: Child NAAT-negative, source rpoB S450L. Treat the child as:
choices: RR-TB using a pediatric DR construct, not HRZE
No treatment because Ultra was negative
check.answer: RR-TB using a pediatric DR construct, not HRZE
check.why: Source genotype is the child’s DST when specimens fail.

check.prompt: On the pediatric treatment hierarchy, BPaLM is listed how for RR <14?
choices: As “not routine BPaLM,” with BDLLfxC as the named 6-month alternative
check.answer: As “not routine BPaLM,” with BDLLfxC as the named 6-month alternative
